messages.content: What is next.jdbc and how do I connect to a database?

next.jdbc is the modern Clojure JDBC library. It's the successor to clojure.java.jdbc with better performance and design.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {com.github.seancorfield/next.jdbc {:mvn/version "1.3.894"}
        ;; Add your database driver
        org.postgresql/postgresql {:mvn/version "42.6.0"}
        ;; Or MySQL
        com.mysql/mysql-connector-j {:mvn/version "8.2.0"}
        ;; Or SQLite
        org.xerial/sqlite-jdbc {:mvn/version "3.44.1.0"}}}

(require '[next.jdbc :as jdbc]
         '[next.jdbc.result-set :as rs])
```

**Datasource Connection**
```clojure
;; Define db spec
(def db-spec
  {:dbtype "postgresql"
   :dbname "mydb"
   :host "localhost"
   :port 5432
   :user "postgres"
   :password "secret"})

;; Create datasource (reusable, connection pooled)
(def ds (jdbc/get-datasource db-spec))

;; Or with JDBC URL
(def ds
  (jdbc/get-datasource
    {:jdbcUrl "jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb?user=postgres&password=secret"}))
```

**Connection Pooling with HikariCP**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {com.zaxxer/HikariCP {:mvn/version "5.1.0"}}}

(require '[next.jdbc.connection :as connection])
(import '[com.zaxxer.hikari HikariDataSource])

;; Create pooled datasource
(def ds
  (connection/->pool HikariDataSource
    {:dbtype "postgresql"
     :dbname "mydb"
     :username "postgres"
     :password "secret"
     ;; Pool settings
     :maximumPoolSize 10
     :minimumIdle 2
     :connectionTimeout 30000}))

;; Important: close on shutdown
(.close ds)

;; Or with component/integrant
(defn start-db [config]
  (connection/->pool HikariDataSource config))

(defn stop-db [ds]
  (.close ds))
```

**Basic Operations**
```clojure
;; Execute SQL (returns modified row count)
(jdbc/execute! ds ["CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100))"])
;; => {:next.jdbc/update-count 0}

;; Execute returning results
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT * FROM users"])
;; => [{:users/id 1 :users/name "Alice"} ...]

;; Execute one (returns first row or nil)
(jdbc/execute-one! ds ["SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?" 1])
;; => {:users/id 1 :users/name "Alice"}

;; Insert
(jdbc/execute! ds ["INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)" "Bob"])

;; Update
(jdbc/execute! ds ["UPDATE users SET name = ? WHERE id = ?" "Robert" 1])

;; Delete
(jdbc/execute! ds ["DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?" 1])
```

**Parameterized Queries**
```clojure
;; Parameters are passed as vector elements after SQL
(jdbc/execute! ds 
  ["SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE ? AND age > ?" 
   "%Alice%" 
   21])

;; Named parameters (with honeysql or hugsql)
;; next.jdbc itself uses positional ? params

;; IN clause
(let [ids [1 2 3]]
  (jdbc/execute! ds
    (into [(str "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN ("
                (clojure.string/join "," (repeat (count ids) "?"))
                ")")]
          ids)))
```

**SQLite Example**
```clojure
(def ds (jdbc/get-datasource {:dbtype "sqlite" :dbname "mydb.sqlite"}))

(jdbc/execute! ds ["CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (
                     id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                     title TEXT NOT NULL,
                     body TEXT,
                     created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"])

(jdbc/execute! ds ["INSERT INTO notes (title, body) VALUES (?, ?)" 
                   "First Note" "Content here"])

(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT * FROM notes"])
```
How do I control result set formatting in next.jdbc?

next.jdbc provides flexible result set handling through builders and options.

**Result Format Options**
```clojure
(require '[next.jdbc :as jdbc]
         '[next.jdbc.result-set :as rs])

;; Default: qualified keywords (table/column)
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT id, name FROM users"])
;; => [{:users/id 1 :users/name "Alice"}]

;; Unqualified keywords
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT id, name FROM users"]
  {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-maps})
;; => [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}]

;; Lower-case + unqualified (most common)
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT ID, NAME FROM users"]
  {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-lower-maps})
;; => [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}]

;; Kebab-case (underscore to dash)
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT user_name, created_at FROM users"]
  {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-kebab-maps})
;; => [{:user-name "Alice" :created-at ...}]
```

**Available Builders**
```clojure
;; Maps (default)
rs/as-maps                    ; {:table/column value}
rs/as-unqualified-maps        ; {:column value}
rs/as-lower-maps              ; {:table/column value} (lowercased)
rs/as-unqualified-lower-maps  ; {:column value} (lowercased)
rs/as-kebab-maps              ; {:table/col-name value}
rs/as-unqualified-kebab-maps  ; {:col-name value}

;; Arrays (faster, ordered)
rs/as-arrays                  ; [[col1 col2] [v1 v2] [v3 v4]]
rs/as-unqualified-arrays      ; Same, unqualified column names
```

**Setting Default Options**
```clojure
;; Create datasource with default options
(def ds 
  (jdbc/with-options 
    (jdbc/get-datasource db-spec)
    {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-kebab-maps}))

;; Now all queries use kebab-case by default
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT user_name FROM users"])
;; => [{:user-name "Alice"}]

;; Override per-query
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT user_name FROM users"]
  {:builder-fn rs/as-maps})  ; Back to qualified
```

**Custom Builder**
```clojure
;; Create custom builder
(defn my-builder [rs opts]
  (rs/as-unqualified-lower-maps rs opts))

;; Or compose builders
(require '[camel-snake-kebab.core :as csk])

(defn as-camel-maps [rs opts]
  (let [builder (rs/as-unqualified-maps rs opts)]
    (reify
      rs/RowBuilder
      (->row [_] (transient {}))
      (column-count [_] (rs/column-count builder))
      (with-column [_ row i]
        (let [col-name (csk/->camelCase (rs/get-column-name builder i))
              value (rs/read-column-by-index (rs/get-column builder i) rs i opts)]
          (assoc! row col-name value)))
      (row! [_ row] (persistent! row))
      rs/ResultSetBuilder
      (->rs [_] (transient []))
      (with-row [_ mrs row] (conj! mrs row))
      (rs! [_ mrs] (persistent! mrs)))))
```

**Handling NULL values**
```clojure
;; NULL becomes nil by default
(jdbc/execute-one! ds ["SELECT NULL as value"])
;; => {:value nil}

;; Custom NULL handling
(defn read-column-with-default [col rs idx _opts]
  (let [value (.getObject rs idx)]
    (if (nil? value)
      "N/A"  ; Default for NULL
      value)))

(extend-protocol rs/ReadableColumn
  Object
  (read-column-by-index [val rs idx opts]
    (or val "N/A")))
```

**Working with Arrays**
```clojure
;; Arrays are faster for large result sets
(jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT id, name FROM users"] 
  {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-arrays})
;; => [["id" "name"] [1 "Alice"] [2 "Bob"]]

;; First row is column names
(let [[cols & rows] (jdbc/execute! ds ["SELECT * FROM users"]
                      {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-arrays})]
  (map #(zipmap cols %) rows))
```

**Result Set as Reducible**
```clojure
;; plan returns reducible - doesn't realize all rows
(into []
  (comp
    (map :users/name)
    (take 10))
  (jdbc/plan ds ["SELECT * FROM users"]))
;; Only fetches 10 rows from DB

;; Good for large result sets
(transduce
  (map :users/balance)
  +
  0
  (jdbc/plan ds ["SELECT balance FROM accounts"]))
```
How do I use transactions in next.jdbc?

next.jdbc provides simple transaction support via `with-transaction`.

**Basic Transactions**
```clojure
(require '[next.jdbc :as jdbc])

;; with-transaction macro
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
  ;; tx is a transacted connection
  (jdbc/execute! tx ["INSERT INTO accounts (name, balance) VALUES (?, ?)" "Alice" 1000])
  (jdbc/execute! tx ["INSERT INTO accounts (name, balance) VALUES (?, ?)" "Bob" 500]))
;; Commits on success, rolls back on exception

;; Using transacted connection
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
  (let [alice (jdbc/execute-one! tx ["SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE name = ?" "Alice"])
        bob (jdbc/execute-one! tx ["SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE name = ?" "Bob"])]
    (when (> (:accounts/balance alice) 100)
      (jdbc/execute! tx ["UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE name = ?" 100 "Alice"])
      (jdbc/execute! tx ["UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE name = ?" 100 "Bob"]))))
```

**Transaction Options**
```clojure
;; Isolation level
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds {:isolation :serializable}]
  ...)

;; Available isolation levels:
;; :none, :read-uncommitted, :read-committed, :repeatable-read, :serializable

;; Read-only transaction (optimization hint)
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds {:read-only true}]
  (jdbc/execute! tx ["SELECT * FROM reports"]))

;; Rollback only (force rollback even on success)
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds {:rollback-only true}]
  ;; Good for testing - changes are always rolled back
  (jdbc/execute! tx ["INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)" "Test"]))
```

**Manual Rollback**
```clojure
;; Throw exception to rollback
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
  (jdbc/execute! tx ["INSERT INTO orders ..." ...])
  (when (some-validation-fails?)
    (throw (ex-info "Validation failed" {:type :rollback}))))

;; Or use .rollback on connection
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
  (jdbc/execute! tx ["INSERT INTO orders ..." ...])
  (when (some-validation-fails?)
    (.rollback (jdbc/get-connection tx))
    (throw (ex-info "Rolled back" {}))))
```

**Nested Transactions (Savepoints)**
```clojure
;; next.jdbc doesn't support nested with-transaction
;; Use savepoints manually
(jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
  (jdbc/execute! tx ["INSERT INTO main_table ..." ...])
  
  (let [conn (jdbc/get-connection tx)
        savepoint (.setSavepoint conn "inner")]
    (try
      (jdbc/execute! tx ["INSERT INTO secondary_table ..." ...])
      (catch Exception e
        (.rollback conn savepoint)
        (println "Secondary insert failed, continuing...")))))
```

**Transfer Example**
```clojure
(defn transfer! [ds from-id to-id amount]
  (jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds {:isolation :serializable}]
    ;; Check source balance
    (let [from-account (jdbc/execute-one! tx
                         ["SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE" from-id])]
      (when (nil? from-account)
        (throw (ex-info "Source account not found" {:id from-id})))
      
      (when (< (:accounts/balance from-account) amount)
        (throw (ex-info "Insufficient funds" 
                        {:balance (:accounts/balance from-account)
                         :requested amount})))
      
      ;; Perform transfer
      (jdbc/execute! tx
        ["UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?" amount from-id])
      (jdbc/execute! tx
        ["UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?" amount to-id])
      
      ;; Log transaction
      (jdbc/execute! tx
        ["INSERT INTO transfers (from_id, to_id, amount, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, NOW())"
         from-id to-id amount])
      
      {:success true :amount amount})))

;; Usage
(try
  (transfer! ds 1 2 100.00)
  (catch Exception e
    (println "Transfer failed:" (ex-message e))))
```

**Testing with Transactions**
```clojure
;; Test fixture that rolls back all changes
(defn with-rollback-fixture [f]
  (jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds {:rollback-only true}]
    (binding [*test-ds* tx]
      (f))))

(use-fixtures :each with-rollback-fixture)

(deftest test-create-user
  (let [result (create-user! *test-ds* {:name "Test"})]
    (is (some? (:id result)))
    ;; Changes automatically rolled back after test
    ))
```

**Transaction Function Style**
```clojure
;; Sometimes cleaner to pass function
(defn in-transaction [ds f & {:as opts}]
  (jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds opts]
    (f tx)))

;; Usage
(in-transaction ds
  (fn [tx]
    (let [user (create-user! tx user-data)
          profile (create-profile! tx (:id user) profile-data)]
      {:user user :profile profile}))
  :isolation :read-committed)
```
How do I use next.jdbc.sql for simpler SQL operations?

next.jdbc.sql provides friendly functions for common CRUD operations without writing raw SQL.

**Setup**
```clojure
(require '[next.jdbc :as jdbc]
         '[next.jdbc.sql :as sql]
         '[next.jdbc.result-set :as rs])

(def ds (jdbc/get-datasource db-spec))
```

**Insert**
```clojure
;; Insert single row
(sql/insert! ds :users {:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"})
;; => {:users/id 1 :users/name "Alice" :users/email "alice@example.com"}

;; Insert with options
(sql/insert! ds :users 
  {:name "Bob" :email "bob@example.com"}
  {:return-keys true
   :builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-maps})
;; => {:id 2 :name "Bob" :email "bob@example.com"}

;; Insert multiple rows
(sql/insert-multi! ds :users
  [:name :email]
  [["Charlie" "charlie@example.com"]
   ["Diana" "diana@example.com"]])
;; Returns count or generated keys depending on DB

;; Insert multiple with maps
(sql/insert-multi! ds :users
  [{:name "Eve" :email "eve@example.com"}
   {:name "Frank" :email "frank@example.com"}])
```

**Query/Find**
```clojure
;; Find all
(sql/find-by-keys ds :users :all)
;; => [{:users/id 1 :users/name "Alice"} ...]

;; Find by simple criteria
(sql/find-by-keys ds :users {:name "Alice"})
;; => [{:users/id 1 :users/name "Alice" ...}]

;; Find by multiple criteria (AND)
(sql/find-by-keys ds :users {:role "admin" :active true})
;; SELECT * FROM users WHERE role = 'admin' AND active = true

;; With options
(sql/find-by-keys ds :users {:role "user"}
  {:order-by [[:created_at :desc]]
   :limit 10
   :offset 0
   :columns [:id :name :email]
   :builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-kebab-maps})

;; Get by primary key
(sql/get-by-id ds :users 1)
;; => {:users/id 1 ...}

(sql/get-by-id ds :users 1 :id {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-maps})
;; => {:id 1 ...}
```

**Update**
```clojure
;; Update by criteria
(sql/update! ds :users
  {:name "Alicia"}           ; SET clause
  {:id 1})                    ; WHERE clause
;; => {:next.jdbc/update-count 1}

;; Update multiple rows
(sql/update! ds :users
  {:status "inactive"}
  {:last_login nil})
;; UPDATE users SET status = 'inactive' WHERE last_login IS NULL

;; Update with example
(sql/update! ds :users
  {:password_hash "new_hash" :updated_at (java.time.Instant/now)}
  {:id 1})
```

**Delete**
```clojure
;; Delete by criteria
(sql/delete! ds :users {:id 1})
;; => {:next.jdbc/update-count 1}

;; Delete multiple
(sql/delete! ds :sessions {:expired true})

;; Delete all (be careful!)
(sql/delete! ds :temp_data :all)
```

**Query Options**
```clojure
;; All functions accept options map
(def opts 
  {:table-fn str/upper-case      ; Transform table names
   :column-fn str/upper-case     ; Transform column names
   :builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-kebab-maps})

(sql/find-by-keys ds :users {:name "Alice"} opts)

;; Order by
(sql/find-by-keys ds :users :all
  {:order-by [[:created_at :desc] [:name :asc]]})

;; Columns to select
(sql/find-by-keys ds :users :all
  {:columns [:id :name :email]})

;; Limit and offset
(sql/find-by-keys ds :users :all
  {:limit 10 :offset 20})

;; For update (row locking)
(sql/find-by-keys ds :accounts {:id 1}
  {:for :update})
```

**Combining with Raw SQL**
```clojure
;; sql/ functions are convenience wrappers
;; Use raw jdbc/execute! for complex queries

;; Complex WHERE
(jdbc/execute! ds
  ["SELECT * FROM users WHERE created_at > ? AND (role = ? OR role = ?)"
   #inst "2024-01-01" "admin" "moderator"])

;; JOINs
(jdbc/execute! ds
  ["SELECT u.*, p.bio FROM users u
    LEFT JOIN profiles p ON p.user_id = u.id
    WHERE u.active = ?"
   true])

;; Aggregations
(jdbc/execute-one! ds
  ["SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM users WHERE role = ?" "user"])
;; => {:count 42}
```

**CRUD Service Example**
```clojure
(ns myapp.db.users
  (:require [next.jdbc :as jdbc]
            [next.jdbc.sql :as sql]
            [next.jdbc.result-set :as rs]))

(def ^:private opts
  {:builder-fn rs/as-unqualified-kebab-maps})

(defn find-all [ds]
  (sql/find-by-keys ds :users :all opts))

(defn find-by-id [ds id]
  (sql/get-by-id ds :users id :id opts))

(defn find-by-email [ds email]
  (first (sql/find-by-keys ds :users {:email email} opts)))

(defn create! [ds user]
  (sql/insert! ds :users user 
    (merge opts {:return-keys true})))

(defn update! [ds id changes]
  (sql/update! ds :users 
    (assoc changes :updated-at (java.time.Instant/now))
    {:id id}))

(defn delete! [ds id]
  (sql/delete! ds :users {:id id}))

(defn search [ds {:keys [query role page per-page]
                  :or {page 1 per-page 20}}]
  (if query
    (jdbc/execute! ds
      ["SELECT * FROM users WHERE name ILIKE ? ORDER BY name LIMIT ? OFFSET ?"
       (str "%" query "%")
       per-page
       (* (dec page) per-page)]
      opts)
    (sql/find-by-keys ds :users 
      (if role {:role role} :all)
      (merge opts {:order-by [[:name :asc]]
                   :limit per-page
                   :offset (* (dec page) per-page)}))))
```
How do I use HoneySQL with next.jdbc?

HoneySQL lets you write SQL as Clojure data structures, then format them to SQL strings for next.jdbc.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {com.github.seancorfield/next.jdbc {:mvn/version "1.3.894"}
        com.github.seancorfield/honeysql {:mvn/version "2.5.1103"}}}

(require '[next.jdbc :as jdbc]
         '[next.jdbc.sql :as sql]
         '[honey.sql :as hsql]
         '[honey.sql.helpers :as h])
```

**Basic Usage**
```clojure
;; Build query as data
(def query
  {:select [:id :name :email]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:= :active true]})

;; Format to SQL
(hsql/format query)
;; => ["SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE active = ?" true]

;; Execute with next.jdbc
(jdbc/execute! ds (hsql/format query))
```

**Using Helpers**
```clojure
;; Build query with helper functions
(-> (h/select :id :name :email)
    (h/from :users)
    (h/where [:= :active true])
    (h/order-by [:name :asc])
    (h/limit 10)
    hsql/format)
;; => ["SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE active = ? ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT ?" true 10]

;; Compose queries
(defn base-user-query []
  (-> (h/select :*)
      (h/from :users)))

(defn active-users []
  (-> (base-user-query)
      (h/where [:= :active true])))

(defn search-users [query]
  (-> (active-users)
      (h/where [:ilike :name (str "%" query "%")])
      (h/order-by [:name :asc])))
```

**WHERE Clauses**
```clojure
;; Comparison operators
[:= :id 1]              ; id = 1
[:!= :status "deleted"] ; status != 'deleted'
[:< :age 30]            ; age < 30
[:> :price 100]         ; price > 100
[:>= :quantity 0]       ; quantity >= 0
[:<= :score 100]        ; score <= 100

;; LIKE
[:like :name "A%"]      ; name LIKE 'A%'
[:ilike :name "%test%"] ; name ILIKE '%test%' (case insensitive, PostgreSQL)

;; NULL
[:= :deleted_at nil]    ; deleted_at IS NULL
[:!= :email nil]        ; email IS NOT NULL

;; IN
[:in :status ["active" "pending"]]  ; status IN ('active', 'pending')

;; BETWEEN
[:between :age 18 65]   ; age BETWEEN 18 AND 65

;; Compound conditions
[:and 
  [:= :active true]
  [:> :age 18]]

[:or
  [:= :role "admin"]
  [:= :role "moderator"]]

;; Complex
[:and
  [:= :active true]
  [:or
    [:= :role "admin"]
    [:and
      [:= :role "user"]
      [:= :verified true]]]]
```

**INSERT**
```clojure
;; Single row
(-> (h/insert-into :users)
    (h/values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}])
    hsql/format)
;; => ["INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)" "Alice" "alice@example.com"]

;; Multiple rows
(-> (h/insert-into :users)
    (h/values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}
               {:name "Bob" :email "bob@example.com"}])
    hsql/format)

;; Insert with columns
(-> (h/insert-into :users [:name :email])
    (h/values [["Alice" "alice@example.com"]
               ["Bob" "bob@example.com"]])
    hsql/format)

;; RETURNING (PostgreSQL)
(-> (h/insert-into :users)
    (h/values [{:name "Alice"}])
    (h/returning :id :created_at)
    hsql/format)
;; => ["INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?) RETURNING id, created_at" "Alice"]
```

**UPDATE**
```clojure
(-> (h/update :users)
    (h/set {:name "Alicia" :updated_at [:now]})
    (h/where [:= :id 1])
    hsql/format)
;; => ["UPDATE users SET name = ?, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = ?" "Alicia" 1]

;; Increment
(-> (h/update :products)
    (h/set {:stock [:- :stock 1]})
    (h/where [:= :id 123])
    hsql/format)
;; => ["UPDATE products SET stock = stock - ? WHERE id = ?" 1 123]
```

**DELETE**
```clojure
(-> (h/delete-from :users)
    (h/where [:= :id 1])
    hsql/format)
;; => ["DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?" 1]
```

**JOINs**
```clojure
(-> (h/select :u.* :p.bio :p.avatar)
    (h/from [:users :u])
    (h/left-join [:profiles :p] [:= :p.user_id :u.id])
    (h/where [:= :u.active true])
    hsql/format)
;; => ["SELECT u.*, p.bio, p.avatar FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN profiles AS p ON p.user_id = u.id WHERE u.active = ?" true]

;; Multiple joins
(-> (h/select :o.id :u.name :p.title)
    (h/from [:orders :o])
    (h/join [:users :u] [:= :u.id :o.user_id])
    (h/join [:products :p] [:= :p.id :o.product_id])
    hsql/format)
```

**Aggregations**
```clojure
(-> (h/select :%count.* :role)
    (h/from :users)
    (h/group-by :role)
    (h/having [:> :%count.* 5])
    hsql/format)
;; => ["SELECT COUNT(*), role FROM users GROUP BY role HAVING COUNT(*) > ?" 5]

;; Multiple aggregates
(-> (h/select :category
              [:%count.* :total]
              [:%avg.price :avg_price]
              [:%sum.quantity :total_quantity])
    (h/from :products)
    (h/group-by :category)
    (h/order-by [:total :desc])
    hsql/format)
```

**Helper Function**
```clojure
(defn query! [ds sql-map & [opts]]
  (jdbc/execute! ds (hsql/format sql-map) opts))

(defn query-one! [ds sql-map & [opts]]
  (jdbc/execute-one! ds (hsql/format sql-map) opts))

;; Usage
(query! ds
  {:select [:*]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:= :active true]})
```
